root_cause.text: `digital_in_recv_sdd_res()` in the NFC Digital `nfcid1` anti-collision handler failed to enforce the `NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE` limit while appending peer-controlled SDD/SEL cascade bytes, allowing a malicious NFC-A target to drive `target->nfcid1_len` past the heap-allocated `struct nfc_target` buffer and cause an out-of-bounds write.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (target->nfcid1_len + size > NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE) { ... rc = -EPROTO; goto exit; }` immediately before `memcpy(target->nfcid1 + target->nfcid1_len, ...)`, and the CVE text states that “the number of cascade rounds is controlled entirely by the peer device” and that “nothing in the driver actually enforces” the three-cascade/10-byte limit.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: `digital_in_recv_sdd_res()` in the NFC Digital `nfcid1` anti-collision handler failed to enforce the `NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE` limit while appending peer-controlled SDD/SEL cascade bytes, allowing a malicious NFC-A target to drive `target->nfcid1_len` past the heap-allocated `struct nfc_target` buffer and cause an out-of-bounds write.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (target->nfcid1_len + size > NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE) { ... rc = -EPROTO; goto exit; }` immediately before `memcpy(target->nfcid1 + target->nfcid1_len, ...)`, and the CVE text states that “the number of cascade rounds is controlled entirely by the peer device” and that “nothing in the driver actually enforces” the three-cascade/10-byte limit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a protocol bounds check to prevent NFCID1 buffer overflow when processing SDD responses.
intent_record.what: A bounds check was inserted before copying additional NFCID1 bytes in `digital_in_recv_sdd_res()`: if `target->nfcid1_len + size` exceeds `NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE`, the code logs `PROTOCOL_ERR("4.7.2.1")`, sets `rc` to `-EPROTO`, and jumps to `exit` instead of performing the `memcpy()` and length update.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents appending more NFCID1 data than the destination buffer can hold. If the incoming SDD response would overflow `target->nfcid1`, the function now aborts cleanly with a protocol error rather than writing past the end of the array.

grouping_result.intent: Add a protocol bounds check to prevent NFCID1 buffer overflow when processing SDD responses.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a bounds check in SDD response handling to prevent NFCID1 length from exceeding the maximum and causing an out-of-bounds write.

candidates.rationale: This append copies peer-controlled NFCID1 cascade bytes into the fixed-size target buffer without a preceding NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE bounds check, enabling overflow.
This length update lets the accumulated NFCID1 length grow past the allocated buffer size when the preceding copy overflows the limit.

vuln_statements.explanation: This append copies peer-controlled NFCID1 cascade bytes into the fixed-size target buffer without checking that target->nfcid1_len stays within NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE, enabling the out-of-bounds write.
This length accumulation advances the tracked NFCID1 size without enforcing the maximum buffer limit, allowing the overflow condition to persist and worsen after the unchecked copy.

The code appends peer-controlled NFCID1 bytes with `memcpy(target->nfcid1 + target->nfcid1_len, sdd_res->nfcid1 + offset, size);` and then increments `target->nfcid1_len += size;` with no check against `NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE` or any other bound. This matches the root cause: a malicious NFC-A target can drive `target->nfcid1_len` past the allocated buffer and cause an out-of-bounds write. There is no fix in this snippet, since the only logic shown is the unchecked append; no maximum-length enforcement or overflow guard is present.
